title: Solving
description: One solve per problem (decision 0010), named by the problem's id. Starting calls return at once; what happens comes as events. Sliding and stacking problems are refused (unsupported).

solve.start.summary: Solves from the start, dropping what the problem holds of earlier solving.

solve.prepare.summary: Drops what the problem holds, builds the search (placements, reduce) and pauses.

solve.continue.summary: Carries on a paused solve, one saved in the file, or an unsolved problem from the start.

solve.pause.summary: Asks the run to pause where it can be continued; nothing is lost. Does not wait: solve.state 'paused' follows. Refused when no run is under way.

solve.savePoint.summary: Asks the assembly search alone to pause where the solve can be saved; the take-aparts under way finish, then 'paused'. The autosave: save, then solve.continue.

solve.abort.summary: The hard stop of a solve under way (a run active, or paused in memory): throws it away (results, paused state, saved position) and waits for the run to end. Refused (invalid_state) when the problem has no such solve, so a finished run's solutions are never lost by a late click: remove them with solution.delete {which: all}, which can be undone; a paused solve from a file is carried on with solve.continue or started over with solve.start. Two document.changed follow: the abort's own, then the run's end from the poll.

solve.status.summary: Where the solve stands, its statistics, and why it failed.

solve.exportPaused.summary: Writes a paused solve as a .btsolve file (the original's BTSOLVE2: the puzzle and the problem's number) to carry it on elsewhere.

solve.importPaused.summary: Opens a .btsolve file as a new, untitled document (the open one goes as with document.new); solve.continue on the problem carries the solve on.

solve.state.summary: A solve's state changed, as the engine's poll saw it: states a run passes through within one poll (50 ms) are skipped, the last state of a run (finished, paused, error, or idle after an abort) is always sent, and it comes before the document.changed that gives the run's end its revision. A client waits for that revision, not the state, before reloading the lists. The problems of a document that is replaced get a last 'idle' after the replacing call's reply.

solve.progress.summary: Where a running solve stands; at most four times a second, and once when a run ends (after its last solve.state). The live counters of the Solver card (assemblies, solutions, time) come from here.

solve.solutionsAdded.summary: The saved solutions changed while solving (new ones, or the list thinned or re-sorted): page them again. At most four times a second, and once when the run ends; the last one of a run carries the final count. The counts are those at the time; the live counters are solve.progress's.
